exposure: Gestational weight gain/loss categories (weight loss, 0-4.9 kg gain, 5-9.09 kg gain [reference], >=9.1 kg gain)
cohort: The study included 16,808 obese women (BMI >= 30 kg/m2) who delivered a full-term singleton in cephalic presentation in Quebec from 2008 to 2011.
finding: A gestational weight gain/loss of less than 5 kg in obese women was associated with a reduced risk of major neonatal morbidity, minor maternal morbidity, preeclampsia/eclampsia, cesarean delivery, and assisted vaginal delivery compared to gaining within recommendations (5-9.09 kg).
mod_finding: Weight gain of 0-4.9 kg was associated with a reduction in assisted vaginal delivery, while weight loss was associated with a reduction in cesarean delivery, and weight gain above recommendations increased the risk of cesarean delivery.
